headline: Highest risk is medium data leakage and capability conflict from shared workspace/MCP use; no direct prompt-injection or compliance breach is evidenced.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cline reads and writes workspace files and uses MCP, while haystack also uses MCP and broad network egress. That creates a plausible instruction-injection bridge if haystack ingests Cline-produced content or shared files as prompts. The profiles do not prove a direct parser path, so uncertainty is escalated to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF haystack consumes workspace files or MCP payloads produced by Cline as instructions, injection is possible.
IF the two agents share an MCP server without provenance checks, attacker-controlled content can steer downstream behavior.
mitigations: Disable shared MCP endpoints for the pair.
Route Cline outputs through a read-only handoff file.
Add a provenance tag to every MCP message.
Require manual review before haystack executes any instruction-like text.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and schema validation at the bridge.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cline touches source code and browser screenshots and has broad network egress; haystack also has broad network egress and can call REST/MCP APIs. If they share a workspace, sensitive code or screenshots can flow into haystack outputs or external services. The profiles do not show a shared workspace explicitly, so this is inferred and kept at medium.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace directory, Cline artifacts can be exposed to haystack.
IF haystack forwards retrieved context to external APIs, workspace contents may leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent.
Remove secrets and screenshots before handoff.
Block haystack from sending raw context to external APIs.
Use a redaction step on files shared between agents.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cline can write the filesystem, modify git state, and run shell commands in a per-workspace session; haystack can also use MCP and broad network egress. Because Cline explicitly shares state via filesystem across instances, overlapping writes to the same repo can race and corrupt git or files. This is a default-dangerous interaction with potentially irreversible repo damage.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same repository or workspace, file and git races can occur.
IF haystack uses MCP tools that mutate shared resources, concurrent updates can conflict with Cline.
mitigations: Assign separate branches per agent.
Pause one agent before the other writes.
Use git locks or a single-writer policy.
Review diffs before merge.
requires-engineering: add workspace-level locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cline can generate code, browser-derived content, and filesystem changes; haystack can consume MCP/REST inputs and produce downstream outputs. If haystack treats Cline output as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade into incorrect retrieval results or actions. The profiles do not show autonomous action-taking by haystack, so medium is the appropriate ceiling.
conditions: IF haystack ingests Cline-generated text without validation, hallucinations or bad code can propagate.
IF haystack triggers downstream workflows from Cline outputs, the error chain widens.
mitigations: Require a verification step before haystack uses Cline output.
Compare outputs against source files or tests.
Limit haystack to retrieval-only mode for shared tasks.
Flag low-confidence Cline outputs for review.
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks.

E_compliance.rationale: Both agents are open-source and the profiles show no explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch. Cline handles model-provider API keys and browser screenshots, while haystack only lists anonymous usage statistics. With no documented compliance divergence, only a low residual risk remains, and the other agent is not separately cited because no mismatch is evidenced.
conditions: IF Cline screenshots contain regulated data and are sent to a noncompliant backend, compliance risk increases.
IF haystack is configured to retain shared inputs longer than Cline's workspace policy, retention mismatch appears.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in screenshots.
Confirm backend retention settings.
Document data-class handling for both agents.
Delete shared artifacts after use.
requires-engineering: align retention and residency policies.
